claims.claim_text: The indexed James P. Baxter III is Williams College president and historian James Phinney Baxter III, the first COI Director of Research and Analysis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact surname, first name, middle initial, suffix, Williams presidency, and NARA appointment record align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the distinctive suffix and exact institutional and government chronology substantially reduce namesake risk.
claims.temporal_assessment: Williams employment began in 1937; NARA dates the COI appointment to July 31, 1941.
claims.match_notes: The Box 43 file has not been reviewed. A Williams page imprecisely calls Baxter OSS Director; the dataset follows NARA's administrative history and preserves that discrepancy in source notes.

claims.claim_text: James Phinney Baxter III's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Office of the Coordinator of Information, where he directed Research and Analysis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA dates Baxter's COI appointment to July 31, 1941 and records that the remaining COI units became OSS on June 13, 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, suffix, and documented office align with the index.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate institutional succession from COI to OSS.
claims.match_notes: COI is modeled as a government assignment rather than a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: James Phinney Baxter III's last civilian employer before his COI and OSS work was Williams College, where he was president and took wartime leave.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Williams records a 1937-1961 presidency and a leave to head Research and Analysis; NARA dates the intervening COI appointment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the distinctive name, suffix, and presidency match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly documented leave; COI intervened immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: The continuing college appointment is not mislabeled as the immediate pre-OSS organization.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Saul K. Padover is historian Saul Kussiel Padover, a Department of the Interior official who performed OSS intelligence work in Europe.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name, P-6 index grade, federal employment chronology, and NYPL description of OSS work align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name and coherent government-to-OSS sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Interior service is documented through 1943, followed by wartime OSS work.
claims.match_notes: The Box 580 personnel file remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Saul Padover's best-supported immediate and last civilian pre-OSS employer was the Department of the Interior, where his official title was Assistant to the Secretary.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1943 Official Register supplies the exact title; the NYPL finding aid dates Interior service from 1938 through 1943 and then describes OSS work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact distinctive name and consistent wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded at year precision; no intervening employer is documented.
claims.match_notes: The contemporary register corrects the finding aid's shorthand 'Assistant Secretary' title.

claims.claim_text: The indexed C. Martin Wilbur is historian Clarence Martin Wilbur, a Field Museum curator who joined OSS Research and Analysis in May 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive indexed form, museum byline and title, and NARA's exact pre-OSS chronology align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; the initial, middle name, rare surname, occupation, and timing corroborate one another.
claims.temporal_assessment: A February 1943 museum publication precedes NARA's May 1943 OSS start.
claims.match_notes: The Box 836 personnel file remains unreviewed; no rank or grade appears in the index.

claims.claim_text: C. Martin Wilbur's immediate and last civilian pre-OSS employer was the Field Museum of Natural History, where he was Curator of Chinese Archaeology and Ethnology.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary museum publication gives Wilbur's curatorial title in February 1943; NARA says he worked with the museum before joining OSS in May.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; distinctive name and aligned professional chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence, with month-level OSS transition.
claims.match_notes: The employment start date is not supplied and is left blank.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Charles F. Remer is the University of Michigan economist who led COI and OSS Far East research.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name, P-8 grade, contemporary university reporting, and NARA's direct link to the named RG 226 personnel file align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through the named NARA personnel-file identifier and corroborating contemporary institutional evidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: University leave and COI work are documented by October-November 1941; later OSS division leadership is documented by NARA.
claims.match_notes: NARA identifies Charles F. Remer Personnel File, NAID 2184121; the physical or digitized file itself has not yet been reviewed for this project.

claims.claim_text: Charles Remer's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Office of the Coordinator of Information, where he headed Far East research.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Contemporary University of Michigan reporting places Remer in COI in 1941-1942; NARA identifies the same office as OSS's predecessor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through exact-name contemporary reporting and NARA's named personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit institutional succession from COI to OSS in June 1942.
claims.match_notes: COI is modeled as a government assignment and is not counted as Remer's civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Charles Remer's last civilian employer before COI and OSS was the University of Michigan, where he was a professor of economics.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: University reporting identifies Remer as an economics professor granted leave for COI work; NARA later calls him a former Michigan professor in COI.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; COI intervened immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: The evidence supports leave from the faculty rather than an inferred permanent separation.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Morris Janowitz is the Department of Justice researcher drafted into the Army in 1943 and assigned to OSS Research and Analysis.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, second-lieutenant index rank, 1943 draft, and OSS R&A assignment align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; multiple specific identifiers extend beyond the name.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional chronology places Justice employment before the 1943 draft and OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: The full service number is retained privately and excluded from this public claim. The Box 370 file remains unreviewed.

claims.claim_text: Morris Janowitz's immediate pre-OSS status was a United States Army assignment following his 1943 draft.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Chicago says Janowitz was drafted in 1943 and assigned to OSS R&A; the index lists him as a second lieutenant.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, year, rank, and assignment align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence from draft into Army assignment and then OSS duty.
claims.match_notes: The Army is modeled as a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Morris Janowitz's last civilian employer before the Army and OSS was the Department of Justice Special War Policies Unit.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Chicago chronology places Special War Policies Unit employment after his 1941 graduation and until his 1943 draft.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; distinctive name and aligned rank and wartime assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly identified as the civilian position held until the intervening military draft.
claims.match_notes: The finding aid does not supply a more specific job title, so none is invented.

claims.claim_text: Morris Janowitz attended Washington Square College of New York University from 1937 to 1941 and earned a bachelor's degree in economics.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Chicago finding aid documents the institution, dates, degree, and field before his Justice Department employment.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar student status, not employment.
claims.match_notes: New York University is not counted as an employer in analytics.
